chapter: Technique, jam sessions, audiences and records
title: Rhythm section of Smith's 1938 bands; Hadnott and Abe Bolar
summary: Smith names guitarist Crook, pianist Emile Williams, McShann on piano in the big band, bassist Hadnott and Abe Bolar, and talks of Hadnott's recent visit.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Was Charles Goodwin the guitar player?
Yeah. Crook. Played guitar. He worked in both bands.
And the piano player?
The piano player was Emile Williams.
And the drummer?
Let me see, who played drums... I had two or three drums around then. But mostly... McShann was in the big band.
Oh, really?

Yeah. He played piano for me in the big band most of the time. Because Emile, he didn't want to go out of town. He was an uptown piano player, one of them fine piano players, you know. Played that soothing, good music. He was a good piano player. Read everything. He played in theatre for years and years, him and another fellow.
And let me see, who was on drums. I don't know what...
Buster Smith - 121
...[INAUDIBLE NAME]... on drums.
He was the Blue Devils' drummer.
Mmm-hmm.
Is he still living?
Yeah! He's still living. Sure is. Don't look a day older.
And the bass player?
The bass player at one time was Hadnott? You ever heard of Hadnott?
Billy Hadnott?
No, no, I forgot his first name. All we called him was Hadnott. He lived in Los Angeles. Somebody said he's still out there playing.
You didn't have Abe Bolar.
No. Abe wasn't in the band. No, Hadnott. Abe was with the Blue Devils. I think Abe got with George Lee or some other fellow after we came back. The Blue Devils broke up, and we all got back...
He's the bass player on that record I played you -- the J.P. Johnson.
Is he?
Yeah. He's the bass player with you and Lips. The J.P. Johnson and Joe Turner.
It might be. He was here the other week.
Buster Smith - 122
Really?
Yeah. He came in, come in and sit right at that table, him and wife.
Good heavens.
Yeah. I hadn't seen him since '43. Heh-heh.
He lives in St. Louis, doesn't he?
No. He lives in Oklahoma City.
Oh, really?
Mmm-hmm, he lives in Oklahoma City. His wife had some sister over here in Fort Worth, and they came over to visit, and he called me to see if he could come on by here.
You know who I spoke to on the phone the other day?
Who?
Snake White.
You talked to him?
Yeah.
Where is he at?
He's at a place called Perry...
[PAUSE]
